newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after rangebound session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after rangebound session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended a touch higher after a thinly-traded, rangebound session with LME closed Monday because of a U.K. public holiday.
"It seems as though copper is acting a little tired," Lawson Spence of Smith Barney said.

After large nearby short long positions on LME were apparently matched last week causing the LME cash to three months backwardation to collapse, the sense of urgency has been removed from the market, Spence said.
"Every time urgency goes away, people then focus on further down the time curve where we will almost certainly see steadily increasing supplies," Spence said.
COMEX July copper settled 0.20 cent firmer at 110.45 cents per pound, traded 110.55 to 109.70 cents. Spot May went out 0.10 cent higher at 111.80 cents.
A new round of strike talks at Chile's Quebrada Blanca copper mine ended without agreement on Sunday as workers held out for special compensation for working at high altitude.
The indefinite strike will continue, union leaders said Sunday.
Chile's Escondida said a strike at the mine, the world's largest, which ended Friday, had not affected production or shipment levels.
